correctness.rationale: The height-two source splits into minimal-side points L and the remaining maximal-side points U, so every strict relation is L-to-U. Lowering top-two-level images on L to level h-2 preserves every relation; then lowering top-level images on U to level h-1 also preserves every relation because all their strict lower neighbors now lie below level h-1. The resulting map avoids the top level and is pointwise below a top-level constant. The standard finite-Alexandroff fact that pointwise-comparable maps are homotopic gives the displayed comparison fence. The four-point two-level crown has order complex S1, so its identity cannot be null-homotopic.
risks: Only null-homotopy of maps/path-connectedness of the mapping space is proved; contractibility of the mapping space is not claimed.

value.rationale: The result gives a uniform structural homotopy collapse for every finite bipartite-poset incidence pattern and identifies the sharp target-level threshold. This is a natural finite-space mapping theorem rather than a small computational instance.

final_claim: Every continuous map from a finite T0-space of height at most two into an ordinal sum of at least three nonempty antichains is null-homotopic; a two-level target does not suffice in general.
limitations: Target is an ordinal sum of nonempty antichains.
